To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and described the mouse cDNA and gene coding for the mouse cartilage-associated protein, a novel developmentally-regulated protein expressed in embryonic cartilaginous tissues, and that this gene belongs to a family of genes that includes genes coding for some nuclear antigents.
we have identified a novel protein, the cartilage-associated protein (CASP) and have isolated and characterized the corresponding cDNAs from chick and mouse.
the mouse CASP gene has been isolated, the protein sequence has been determined, the gene has been mapped and the protein has been shown to be expressed in mouse embryonic cartilage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel protein expressed in cartilaginous tissues during mouse development and its possible involvement in the process of chondrogenesis.
the isolation of a novel gene family, which includes genes coding for proteins expressed in cartilage and some nuclear antigens.
a new protein, the CASP, which is expressed during mouse embryonic development and is homologous with a protein that has been identified as a nuclear antigen in chick embryos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Crtap gene is a novel member of a family of genes encoding proteins with a high degree of sequence identity and that the Crtap gene product is an evolutionarily conserved cartilage associated protein.
the mouse and chick cartilage associated proteins are homologous and belong to a novel gene family.
the CASP protein is expressed in a developmentally regulated manner during mouse embryogenesis and is expressed in all embryonic mouse cartilages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CASP is a novel protein expressed in cartilage during development and that the CASP protein belongs to a novel family of nuclear antigens.
we have identified a new protein family that includes the cartilage-associated protein, and the nuclear antigens NuMA and NuBP1.
the CASP gene belongs to a novel gene family that is conserved during evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CASP is a highly conserved molecule that is expressed in a tissue-specific manner and that it is encoded by a gene that is located at a conserved region of the mammalian genome.
the cartilage associated protein is conserved in vertebrates and it is a member of a new gene family.
the mouse Crtap gene is highly expressed during cartilage development and that its expression is restricted to cartilages.
